subject: Re: Competitive eval \u0014 model quality follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (model quality comparison)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sarah  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so were aligned:

What we heard from Acme:
- Primary focus: minimize hallucinations for customer-facing summarization and reduce regression risk when we update models.
- SLOs: <5% hallucination rate (user-visible factual errors) on high-value summaries; latency target ~300ms p95 for production workloads.
- Constraints: must compare Redwood hosted offering vs. your current hyperscaler provider (CloudCorp API) on the same prompt set and business examples.

Redwood proposed plan:
1) We’ll run a side-by-side model quality eval using the prompts we discussed. Attached is the initial prompt set (acme-eval-prompt-set.csv).
2) Metrics we’ll report: hallucination rate (manual + automated detection), factual precision, answer completeness, and regression diffs vs your incumbent baseline.
3) We’ll run tests on the same model variants you care about (e.g., Mistral-like open model and a quantized variant we expect you’ll run in production).
4) Kickoff: propose Monday 8/24 for test start, deliver initial results 48h after kickoff.

Action items:
- Acme: confirm kickoff date and flag any sensitive prompts you don’t want shared beyond our evaluation team.
- Redwood: run the eval, share a short dashboard + PDF summary (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-metrics.pdf).

Attachments:
- acme-eval-prompt-set.csv (initial prompt set)

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) and Neha (ML lead) to finalize the harness.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah  looping in the test/SE plan below so it’s explicit. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Eval harness (high level):
- Dataset: acme-eval-prompt-set.csv (you’ll see categorized prompts: summary, extraction, Q/A, multi-turn).
- Models: Redwood-hosted open model (rwd-open-13B, float32) and quantized variant (rwd-open-13B-int8). Incumbent: CloudCorp GPT-infer v2.
- Metrics: hallucination_rate_auto (lexical inconsistency + NER-backed entity-check), hallucination_rate_manual (sample adjudication n=200), factual_precision, BLEU-like relevance, completeness score, p95 latency.
- Regression checks: diffing model outputs with normalized tokenization and answer normalization; flag regressions >5% on critical prompts.
- Statistical significance: bootstrap CIs for primary metrics.

What we need from Acme before kickoff:
- Temporary evaluation API key for your CloudCorp account (read-only testing scope) OR a sample export of CloudCorp outputs if you prefer not to share keys.
- Confirmation on the 8 restricted prompts and where those must run (hosted vs private).
- A primary contact for adjudication (one product SME + one engineering SME) to review the manual sample within 48h of delivery.

Deliverables and timeline:
- 8/24: Test kickoff and environment validation (Redwood will validate parity with CloudCorp).
- 8/26: Initial results + PDF summary (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-metrics.pdf) and a short recording of the run.
- 8/27: Manual adjudication results and recommended remediation steps if we see regressions.

Attachments: we’ll attach the test harness README and the expected output schema to the HubSpot drive link.

Thanks,

Adding a couple technical clarifications from product/ML so expectations are set: 

1) Model variants: the quantized variant (int8) can introduce small differences in hallucination behavior. We’ll include both float32 and int8 runs and label them clearly in the deliverable.
2) Prompt framing: small prompt rewrites can materially change hallucination rates. We’ll run two framing variants per prompt (original + conservative framing) so you can see sensitivity.
3) Hallucination detection: our automated pipeline flags candidate hallucinations via NER/entity mismatch + knowledge-base grounding checks; we always surface a manual sample for adjudication. For the manual sample we recommend focusing on 100 high-value summaries and 100 random items for statistical balance.
4) Regression thresholds: to avoid noise we’ll flag regressions that exceed 5 percentage points in hallucination_rate_manual or 7 percentage points in factual_precision.

I’ve uploaded a short internal test run we did against a synthetic dataset  link here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-harness (contains README, schema, and a sample run).

If Acme is comfortable we’ll include the six restricted prompts in a private-only test run; let us know if you prefer a Private deployment for those.

-Neha
